name: AliasOrigin
description: Where a name came from. Four values rather than two, because the origin answers two questions that do not move together: whether the member has answered the naming question at all, and whether the name cost one of their picks.

values.name: ASSIGNED
values.description: The system built the name and the member has not answered yet.

values.name: MIGRATED
values.description: An assigned name that migration 0116 handed out. Kept apart only so that migration's rollback takes back its own work; behaves like assigned everywhere else.

values.name: CHOSEN
values.description: The member typed it themselves. The only value that costs one of ALIAS_QUOTA_PER_WINDOW.

values.name: ADOPTED
values.description: The member kept the name the system built. That is an answer, not a pick, so it costs nothing.

notes: settled answers 'has the member answered the question the first-login window asks'. countsAgainstQuota answers 'does it spend one of the four picks a year'. Conflating them charged a member a quarter of their yearly quota for a name nobody chose.
An implementation that counts rows in user_aliases instead of counting the ones with countsAgainstQuota is wrong, in exactly that way.
